served CT frame throughput through E (R244-02): with every frame response its own B2 access record a frame held the 4 append lanes 233 ms median (run e-route-diag2-opus-20261026a). The record is now the study delivery (20261027090000): per frame one bounded ledger transaction for the current access check and plan, the frame's own rows on the application connection, no admission, append or terminal event per frame. Same VM, same 200 x 512x512 CT, both integrated with #248 c99f45b (runs e-route-before-fable-20261027a on 1a95c94, e-route-after-fable-20261027a on bb2b3c8): first opening 9.1 s first image / 19.4 s all frames before, 10.5 / 17.3 s after; repeated opening 4.1 / 14.5 s before, 4.2 / 11.6 s after (19.3 -> 27.2 frames/s after the first image), against 4.2 / 7.8 s direct (e-route-red3-opus-20261026a). The per-stage profile (run e-route-diag-fable-20261027a, 405 responses, medians) showed the four lanes saturated again: the identity admission waited 222 ms and the one ledger transaction 285 ms, with D's per-frame current read running an Orthanc QIDO inside the lane while Orthanc serves the frames; staging 126 ms; the viewer keeps about 20 frames in flight. With the per-response re-check (ImageContextSource.recheck, 323a259: D's scope read and the provision on the lane, the archive's patient identity read once per delivery opening; run e-route-after2-fable-20261027a on fd12aef = 323a259 + #248): first opening 11.3 / 17.8 s, repeated 4.3 / 10.6 s (32.0 frames/s). A repeated opening is 1.36x direct and a first opening 2.2x: not the 1.2x the throughput order asked for. What a frame still pays: the request identity's own append admission (B2), one bounded ledger transaction (D resolves the identity twice, reads StudyState, the StudyAccess snapshot and the FOR SHARE scope), the staging copy and hash of the frame (the same archive read the direct route pays), and three application-connection inserts; the first opening also waits for the whole-study catalog read (#248). Fix round 3 (same VM, CT and stand-in catalog, #248 c99f45b): sample a (e-route-fix3-fable-20261027a; the member id kept once resolved so an established member's request takes no lane, D resolving the identity once per transaction, the study identity read per response) 11.6 / 18.2 s first opening, 4.4 / 11.2 s repeated: no change, so the bound was not where the identity queued; sample b (the per-response check on the application connection instead of a lane) failed outright: the check transaction and the reads D makes outside it waited on the same five-connection pool (Prisma pool timeout); sample c (e-route-fix3-fable-20261027c; the check on E's own eight-connection pool, check-db.ts) 11.2 / 17.2 s first, 4.2 / 10.5 s repeated, 3/3 OK (1.35x warm, 2.16x cold): the same as the previous round, so the lanes were not the bound either. What a frame still pays is shared per-frame work: five archive round trips (object lookup, study identity, header tags, meta header, the raw frame) against one on the direct route, the check's queries, the staging write, hash and read-back, and the API's CPU on the two-vCPU VM; the per-stage profile of this code is run e-route-diag3-fable-20261027a (timing marks on a local branch, never pushed; medians per response: identity 9 ms, the check transaction 140, staging 273 of which three sequential archive reads about 140 before the raw frame, the body to nginx 110, cleanup 90, total 697 ms: 29 frames/s at about twenty in flight, each stage an ordinary round trip inflated by the host, no lane or lock left). Sample d (e-route-fix3-fable-20261027d; a response's archive reads run together and the object's archive id kept per kept manifest, every per-response check unchanged) 11.2 / 17.5 s first, 4.6 / 10.6 s repeated, 3/3 OK: no measurable change (1.37x warm, 2.19x cold). On this two-vCPU VM the ~1.2x target is not reached by E's sequencing; what a frame still pays is the authority check's queries, the raw read and hash before the first byte (E-01/E-02), the body hop through the API, and the host itself. The cold first image is #248's catalog build (about 6 to 7 s): what it must change is written in the round's evidence (spec-248-cold-catalog.md)
